I've been a Windows user for years. I use it for my personal computers and I directly support it at work for my organization. I haven't had any major issues with Microsoft in the past, but Windows 10 introduces a problem I simply can't get around. You see, I have an abysmal bandwidth cap. Data usage has always been my main concern at home, and with no other choice of ISP I have to be very careful of my bandwidth usage and when I update. In the past I've planned my updates around my cap's rollover date, brought my laptop to the office to update, or bummed bandwidth at the local library. But Windows 10 takes those options away from me. Its automatic updates are convoluted and poorly thought out, and takes for granted that everyone has enough bandwidth to spare. You can block specific updates that cause problems, but there's no way to turn off automatic updates completely. You can set a wireless connection as a metered connection, but for some reason you're not allowed to set a wired connection as metered. What's worse, the default setup had my computer set to broadcast itself as an update source, letting other machines use my bandwidth to get updates. All of these hurdles and settings keep bringing me back to the same idea: Microsoft just doesn't care about bandwidth anymore. Without the tools to manage updates the way I need to, Windows just isn't a fit for my environment anymore.
Microsoft just doesn't care about bandwidth anymore (x-post /v/Technology)

In an ideal world, Microsoft no longer caring about bandwidth will force consumers to get angry at ISP's which will then force said ISP's to not care about bandwidth.

In the real world... not so much.

I think the reality is that it doesn't matter how angry users are at their ISP. If the ISP has a stranglehold on the market, there's no option. The government doesn't care unless there's enough uproar, and there won't be any uproar as long as the problem doesn't affect the majority. The problem isn't that people aren't mad at their ISPs; the problem is that the angry minority doesn't have any choice right now.

I think a lot of developers are taking bandwidth for granted now. Websites are getting bloated with images, animations, videos, etc. At least you can block those.

Need help dual booting Linux and Windows 10

Run the windows installer. Format your entire drive. Create a partition of 50% of your drive for windows. Leave the rest unpartitioned. Install onto the partition. Boot into windows, run updates, get set up, etc. Next use Linux Live USB Creator to burn your linux distro. Boot from the USB drive. When you choose to install and it asks you what you want to do, choose "Something else" and then go into the manual format/partition options. Choose to create a new partition from the unpartitioned space. Install onto the new partition and choose "Mount point: /" and click "format". To choose the bootloader, pick the hard drive that houses both OSs (the one that does not have an a, b, c etc. prefix). After installation, remove the USB drive and reboot. You should be presented with a dual boot grub manager where you can choose Windows or Linux. If you don't, then you can get the "boot-repair" linux package and run it with the recommended settings. 99% of the time it fixes the bootloader. I trust boot-repair far more than EasyBCD. If you are blocked out of your linux OS you can always run your USB drive in live mode and install boot-repair in live mode just to get the grub bootloader working correctly.
